title: Case maths trick: percentages in your head
description: Percentages in your head: a quick way to do this case calculation in your head, with a worked example.
hook: Percentages come up in almost every case. Here is a way to work them out in your head quickly, without a calculator.
body:
The problem

What is 15% of 240?

Step by step

  1. 10% = 24
  2. 5% = 12
  3. 24 + 12

Answer: 36.

How to say it in the interview

What is fifteen percent of two hundred and forty?

Start from ten percent: move the decimal one place. Twenty four.

Five percent is half of that: twelve.

Add them: ten plus five is fifteen percent.

So fifteen percent of two hundred and forty is thirty six.

Build any percentage from ten, five and one percent. It is faster, and much harder to get wrong.

Notice that the last step is always about meaning. A number on its own earns half the marks; a number with "so what" earns all of them.
outro: Small things like this add up. Try it in your next practice case and notice how it changes the conversation. Practise sums like this in the free case maths drill.
